rationale: Both run a correct graph search with the right six hex neighbours. B's design is elegant: package-level neighbour offsets, and start/end-edge predicates passed into a single closure. However, it assumes every row has the length of lines[0] and indexes lines[r][c] up to that width, so a ragged board would panic. It also packs the predicates into long one-line lambdas. A checks bounds against each row's own length, rejects invalid characters with an error, and splits the work into small, documented top-level functions (connects, neighbors). Its horizontal boolean flag, with the && / || expressions that depend on it, is slightly less elegant than B's predicates. On balance A is more robust and just as readable.
